# Synthetic Offer and Negotiation Scenarios

All roles, companies, ranges, and circumstances below are fictional test inputs. Numbers test decision behavior only and are not current-market claims.

| Scenario | Synthetic input | Expected behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Good coverage | Senior Software Engineer; multiple recent, comparable fictional sources | Show each attributable evidence row and derive distinct Target range, Preferred outcome, and candidate-defined Fallback without claiming mathematical certainty. |
| Sparse role/location | Specialist role in a small market; one adjacent-role source | Label the adjacent population, lower confidence, widen/qualify the range, and proceed without requiring every optional field. |
| Contradictory sources | Two fictional sources cover different company segments and materially disagree | Preserve both rows, explain population mismatch, and use a conditional position rather than silently averaging. |
| Employer range below target | Employer supplies a range below the evidence-grounded target | Prepare a natural lower-range response that explores flexibility and total compensation without threats or invented leverage. |
| Total compensation changes result | Lower base includes a material fictional bonus/equity package with stated risk and terms | Compare total value, vesting/liquidity/risk, and terms; do not choose on base salary alone. |
| Missing optional information | Role, market, and employer range are known; current compensation and competing offers are omitted | Reuse known context, do not require current compensation or competing offers, state assumptions, and provide useful preparation. |

Each scenario is evaluated at the behavior-contract level. No fixture value may be presented as real or current salary evidence.
